confirmed.description: Marthanda Varma is drawn with grey hair. In 6.4 he stands in the background with his spear, and his hair at the temples and swept back into the knot is plainly silver-grey. In the panels on either side (5.5, 6.3, 7.2, 7.4, 7.5) and on the varma-v1 sheet his hair is jet black. Nothing in the bible greys Varma before the ch28 dedication, so in 1741 he looks about 20 years too old here.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of page-06.png around (1100-1500, 1310-2010): Varma beside the 'I will worry about debts' balloon has grey-white streaked hair. In 6.3 (crop around 880-1180, 910-1180) the same king has black hair.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. At 4x zoom on page-06.png (about x1180-1360, y1350-1520), Varma in 6.4 has a clear band of silver-grey running from the temple back over the ear into the swept-back hair. Only the knot is black. It reads as grey even at one-third scale, so it will show at print size and is not just a highlight. The same king is jet-black in 6.3 (crop around x900-1150, y880-1080) and essentially black in 7.5 (page-07 around x740-920, y2000-2180). On the varma-v1 sheet, grey temples appear only on the LATER DEDICATION figure, so 6.4 looks like it took the late-life version by mistake. Nothing in the bible greys him in chapter 12: his entry and rows (CONTINUITY.md line 76 and the ch7, ch10 and ch11 rows) never mention grey. The script's 6.4 only places Varma in the background. The 'older' note there is for the Nair chieftain in the foreground, who is correctly grey, so he can't be used to justify Varma's grey. Face, moustache, mundu, necklaces and spear all match, so this is not a wrong identity. It is a localized ageing error on one panel, so major, not blocker. Fix: redraw or inpaint Varma's hair in 6.4 to solid black.

confirmed.description: Ramayyan's face drifts from his approved sheet. In this close-up he has a thin moustache and grey stubble on the chin and jaw, and his hair is long, straight and slicked back to the nape. The sheet (03-ramayyan-dalawa-v15) and his other panels (2.1, 3.1, 3.3, 3.5, 6.1, 7.4) show a clean-shaven man with a bald crown and a short ring of tight curls. In the chapter's only tight shot of him he reads as an older, different man.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of page-02.png around (1000-1350, 370-780): a faint moustache, chin and jaw stubble, and long dark hair combed straight back behind the ear. Compare the 2.1 crop (600-800, 460-640): bald crown, curly sides, clean chin.

verdict.reason: The finding holds. In the full-resolution crop of page 2, panel 2.2 (about x 925-1690, y 360-1050), Ramayyan has a clear dark-grey moustache and grey stubble on his upper lip, chin and jaw. His side and back hair is long, loose and wavy, combed back behind the ear. The approved sheet (03-ramayyan-dalawa-v15.png) shows him clean-shaven in every view and expression, with a bald crown and a short ring of tight black curls. His other panels on the same page agree with the sheet: in 2.1 he has tight curls and a clean chin, and in 2.4 his chin and jaw are clean. The moustache is still visible at print size; it shows even on the downscaled full-page view, and the face spans almost an inch in the 6-inch-wide panel. Nothing in the bible or script allows it. The bible gives Ramayyan only "thin, sharp fine features, receding hair" and no facial hair for chapter 12. It also gives Mathoo Tharakan "grey receding hair, a fine grey moustache" so that he "never merges with Ramayyan", which this drawing works against. The script's 2.2 is a tight shot of his hands turning a stone and calls for no change to his look. This is not a blocker: the bald crown, white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus, together with the scene, still identify him. It is a clearly wrong face in one prominent panel, so the right severity is major. The panel needs a redraw of the face, or a recrop onto the hands as the script intends, with a clean-shaven face and tight curls.

confirmed.description: Varma is drawn standing on the dais step with his spear. In 6.3, 7.2 and 7.4 he is seated, and the script saves his rising for 7.5 ("Varma rising, spear in hand"). So he stands up in 6.4, sits down again with no beat between, and the 7.5 rise loses its force.
confirmed.evidence: 6.4 right half: Varma stands full length on the dais, the spear grounded in his right hand. 6.3 and 7.2 show him seated cross-legged on the cushioned seat. In 7.4 he is seated as he hands back the ola.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. In the 6.4 crop (right half), Varma stands full length at the foot of the dais steps. His bare feet are on the mat and his right hand grips the grounded spear. He is also not holding the ola, though he reads it in 6.3 and still has it in 7.2. In 6.3 he sits cross-legged on the red cushioned seat with the leaf in his hands. In 7.2 he is seated with the ola. In 7.4 he is seated again: his draped lap rests on the red cushion as he passes the ola to Ramayyan. 7.5 then shows him standing, spear in hand. The script never has him stand before 7.5. In 6.1 he leans forward "from his seat", in 7.2 he holds the ola "beside his seat", and 7.5 is scripted as "Varma rising, spear in hand". The 6.4 note only asks for Varma in the background, not looking at the chief, so nothing calls for him to stand. CONTINUITY.md says nothing about his posture, and the cast override for 6.4 only says the panel shows Varma alone. So he stands in 6.4, is seated again in 7.2 with no beat in between, and the scripted rise in 7.5 loses its force. The standing figure is large and plain at print size. 6.5, shot over his shoulder, does not show clearly whether he is seated or standing, so it neither fixes nor worsens the break. Severity: major. It is a clear staging error confined to one panel, which needs Varma redrawn seated on the dais, ideally still holding the ola. It does not affect identity, lettering or a missing beat, so it is not a blocker.

confirmed.description: Varma's age drifts: grey streaks appear at his temples, though no ch12 bible row gives him grey. Grey belongs to his later-dedication sheet. It also comes and goes within the war-hall scene.
confirmed.evidence: Zoomed head in 6.4: clear silver strands sweep back from the temple. The same grey strands show in 7.5. His hair is solid black in 5.5, 6.3 and 7.4.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 6, panel 4. Varma is the standing figure on the right, and a broad silver-grey streak sweeps back from his left temple into the side knot. At 4x zoom it is plain. In a native-size crop of the panel (about 1540 px wide at 300 DPI) it still reads clearly as grey at print size. It is not the grey-haired older chieftain in the foreground, whom the script allows.

The bible does not allow it. Varma's base line is the V13 varma-v1 face, and the ch12 @5- row asks only for a bare head with a side knot above the left ear. Neither gives him grey. The only grey-at-the-temple Varma is the LATER DEDICATION figure on varma-v1.png, which is bare-headed with the same swept grey streak. That figure is reserved for ch28, where the row says "same face aged".

The renderer appears to have taken the bare-headed later-dedication look for this scene. In the same continuous war-hall scene his hair is solid black: 5.5, 6.3, 7.2 and 7.4 all checked at 3-4x. So the king's age visibly jumps for one panel.

7.5 shows only a few faint grey strands, visible at 8x and negligible at print size. The real fix is 6.4 alone.

It is major, not a blocker. Varma is still recognisable (same face, moustache, side knot, mundu, necklaces, spear), and the error is one localized age and continuity cue. The fix is to redraw 6.4 with black hair and no grey at the temples.

confirmed.description: The coin beat is missing. The script has Nagoji "setting one plain gold coin on a small stack from the brass tray", which pays off the tray planted in 5.3, 6.2 and 7.2 and shows what a pagoda is. This panel has no tray and no coin.
confirmed.evidence: 7.3 table: only stacked palm-leaf bundles and a small dark ink pot. No brass tray and no gold coins. Nagoji's hands are lost behind the lower balloon. The tray of coins is plainly visible on the table in 7.2, one panel earlier.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on the printed page, but the cause is the lettering and crop, not the drawing. On page 7, panel 3 as rendered (r1/page-07.png), the table shows only the tied palm-leaf bundle and the ink pot with its pen. You cannot see a brass tray, a gold coin or Nagoji's hand on a coin. The tray is plainly visible one panel earlier in 7.2. The unlettered source frame (chapters/ch12/frames/page-07-panel-03-v01.png) does draw the beat: Nagoji's right hand sets a gold coin on a short coin stack, with the brass tray of coins beside it in the middle of the table. The panel is cropped in tight, and the large lower balloon ("The Marathas are patient... every pagoda...") sits right over the middle of the table. Together they hide the hand, the stack and the tray completely. So the script beat (one gold coin set on a stack from the brass tray, which pays off the tray planted in 5.3 and shows what a pagoda is) is lost on the page. It is a localized fix: move or shrink the lower balloon, for example up into the wall area or to the lower right over the foreground chief, or loosen the crop. No redraw is needed. That makes it major (an awkward crop and balloon hiding the action), not a blocker.

confirmed.description: Wrong prop business for Ramayyan. He should be lowering the courier's ola as he turns to Varma. Instead he holds a cord-bound bundle with a stylus poised over it, like his own palm-leaf ledger, so the announcement reads as note-taking.
confirmed.evidence: 5.5 left: his right hand holds a stylus angled onto a bundle tied with twine, matching his sheet's ledger and stylus. In 5.2 the courier's ola is a broad, pale stack sealed with red wax, and he breaks the seal in 5.3.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on a zoomed crop of page 5, panel 5 (left figure). Ramayyan's right hand grips a thin, dark stylus like a pen, with its tip resting on top of a dark, cord-bound stack of leaves. His left hand holds that stack flat at waist height, which is a writing pose. This bundle is not the courier's ola from 5.2, which is a broad, pale stack with a red wax seal; there is no wax and no broken seal. It matches the "palm-leaf bundles and stylus" from his continuity base line instead. Script 5.5 asks for "Ramayyan lowering the leaf and turning to Varma". As drawn, he looks like he is taking notes while he says "Chanda Sahib has fallen.", so the news no longer comes from the letter. The stylus is a clear dark stroke against his white cloth, so it will still read at print size. Nothing in the script or bible allows him to be writing at this moment: the stylus is a general character prop, not this beat's business. Partly related: 5.4 already shows a cord-bound bundle with no wax, darker than the 5.2 ola. In 5.4, though, he is gripping it as the script asks. The stylus pose in 5.5 is what clearly breaks the beat. This is major, not a blocker: the line, the speaker and Varma are all in the panel and the beat is still there, but the prop business is wrong and confined to this one panel. Fix: redraw 5.5 with no stylus and with him lowering the pale, opened ola from 5.2/5.3 as he turns toward Varma.

confirmed.description: Nagoji's boots, set side by side below the shrine steps, are drawn as modern lace-up work or combat boots. They have punched eyelets, crossed shoelaces, rear pull tabs and heavy lug soles. That is an anachronism, and it also breaks from the approved commander sheet, whose boots are soft leather wrapped with thongs. The thong-wrapped version is drawn correctly in 4.2.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of page-02.png at display coords around (108-260, 640-730), zoomed 3x. Both boots show metal-eyelet lacing, a heel pull loop and a thick stitched sole. Compare the thong-wrapped boots in nagoji-v2.png and in 4.2 (page-04.png, around x 370-560, y 1040-1160).

verdict.reason: Confirmed, but as minor rather than major. A 4x crop of page-02.png (full-res x 140-340, y 840-1050) shows the pair of boots below the steps in panel 2.1 with criss-cross front laces tied in bows, rear pull tabs at the top of the shaft, and a stiff welted sole with a cap toe. They read as modern lace-up work or combat boots. The approved nagoji-v2 sheet shows soft mid-calf boots wrapped with thongs around the shaft, and panel 4.2 (page-04.png, around x 470-730, y 1490-1620) draws that version correctly. So 2.1 is off-model, and inside the same chapter. Neither the script (2.1 says only that the boots are off and side by side) nor CONTINUITY ("boots together below the shrine steps") allows a different boot. It is not major, for three reasons. At 300 DPI print size the pair is only about 0.4 in wide, tucked into the lower-left corner beside a balloon. The pull tabs and welts are barely legible at that size. And front lacing alone is not strictly anachronistic for the 1740s. At print a reader sees laced brown boots with a vaguely modern outline: a localized polish fix (redraw them as thong-wrapped soft boots to match the sheet and 4.2), not a clear costume blocker.

confirmed.description: The page has no grid. All five panels are inset by different amounts and centred, so the page reads as a ragged stack of thumbnails, not a comic page like the approved Chapter 1. The script calls 8.5 'Full width, bottom', but it is one of the narrowest rows.
confirmed.evidence: Measured row widths at 300 DPI, against a 1540 px live column (Ch1 r6 rows are 1540 px, with at most a 55 px inset): 8.1 = 1187 px, 8.2 = 733 px (48%), 8.3 = 1071 px, 8.4 = 1128 px, 8.5 = 946 px (61%). The left edges are all different (x = 325, 552, 383, 354, 445), so wide cream gutters show on both sides of every row.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 8. I re-measured the dark panel borders on page-08.png (1838 x 2775 at 300 DPI) and got the same numbers the reviewer gave: 8.1 x=325-1512 (1187 px), 8.2 x=552-1285 (733 px), 8.3 x=383-1454 (1071 px), 8.4 x=354-1482 (1128 px), 8.5 x=445-1391 (946 px). None of the five rows reaches the 1540 px live column (x=148-1688). Ch12 pages 1, 2, 3 and 5, and Ch1 r6 pages 1 to 4, all have rows that do. At print size, 8.2 is about 2.4 in wide on a 5.125 in column, with roughly 1.35 in of extra cream on each side. Because all five left edges differ, the page reads as a ragged, centred stack of thumbnails. You can see it at thumbnail scale.

The script does not allow this. It calls 8.5 "Full width, bottom", but 8.5 is the second-narrowest row at 61% of the column. The cause is the compositor's "contain_visible_viewport_centered_inside_planned_slot" policy, which shrinks each frame to fit its own aspect ratio inside its slot and centres it. That is an engine default, not something the script or the bible approves.

One part of the reviewer's evidence is overstated. Ch1 r6 does have some inset rows: page 4 has a row at 1378 px, an 81 px inset, more than the claimed 55 px maximum. Ch12 pages 4 and 7 also each have two 1091 px rows. So a single narrower row is tolerated elsewhere, but no other page has every row narrow and every left edge different.

Major, not blocker. The art, the lettering and every beat are intact and readable. Only this page's layout is wrong. It can be fixed by re-laying it out (crop or regenerate the frames to fill the column, or pair 8.2 and 8.4 side by side) without redrawing the content.

confirmed.description: Rows 1 and 3 are shrunk to about 71% of the column and centred, while rows 2 and 4 run full width. The page steps in and out with large empty cream margins. The script calls 4.1 'Wide action'.
confirmed.evidence: 4.1 and 4.4 measure 1091 px wide (x 373-1464). 4.2/4.3 and 4.5 measure 1540 px (x 148-1688). The inset is about 225 px a side, against at most 28 px in Ch1 r6.

verdict.reason:
The measurement is correct, but this is minor, not major. On page-04.png, the 4.1 and 4.4 frames run from x 373 to 1464, about 1091 px. The 4.2/4.3 pair and 4.5 run from x 148 to 1688, about 1540 px. That leaves cream bars about 225 px (0.75 in) on each side, so the page visibly steps in and out.

It falls short of major for four reasons:
(1) Nothing is lost. The ravine, the Nair line, Dhanaji, Nagoji and the riders wheeling away in 4.1 are all in frame and uncropped, and so are the parapet, lamp and pennanted column in 4.4. All captions are legible.
(2) The script cues are met. 4.1 asks only for "Wide action", and the art is a landscape frame at 1.92:1. 4.4 has no width cue. The one panel marked "Full width", 4.5, does span the column.
(3) It is the documented layout policy. compositor.fit_clip_contain centres art that is narrower than its slot ("contain_visible_viewport_centered_inside_planned_slot"). review/COMPOSITION-r1.json records both slots as planned 369 pt and placed 261 pt. The bible sets no rule on row width.
(4) The same stepped rows appear in other V15 chapter renders: ch03 r10 p3, ch05 r2 p1 and p7, ch06 r6 p4. So the Ch1 r6 baseline the reviewer cited is not the house norm.

It still counts as a real minor issue. The layout_fit.py docstring treats side bars as under-fill to be reduced where the page budget allows. The polish fix is to shorten rows 1 and 3, or regenerate those frames at about 2.7:1 and 3.2:1, so they span the column.

confirmed.description: The panel grid is broken. 7.1 is shrunk to 71% width and centred. In the second tier, 7.2 and 7.3 sit side by side but have different heights and offsets: 7.3 starts about 30 px higher and ends about 30 px lower than 7.2, so the gutters are uneven and the tier looks misregistered. 7.4 is also inset.
confirmed.evidence: 7.1 is 1091 px wide (x 373-1464) against a 1540 px column. In the crop of the second tier, 7.2's top border sits at about y 55 and its bottom at about y 632, while 7.3's sit at about y 22 and y 663. 7.4 is 1444 px wide (x 196-1640).

verdict.reason: I confirmed part of this, but it is minor, not major. I measured page-07.png at 1838x2775. 7.1 runs x 373-1465 (1092 px) and 7.4 runs x 196-1641 (1445 px), which matches the reviewer's figures. Those insets are not a defect, though. The compositor's policy is to fit each image inside its planned slot and centre it there (pipeline/compositor.py, fit_clip_contain, "contain_visible_viewport_centered_inside_planned_slot"), so narrower centred panels are normal. The same thing shows on page 4 (tier 1 and tier 3 are both x 373-1464), on page 6 (tiers 2 and 4) and on every tier of page 8. That part is refuted. The second tier is a real problem. 7.2 sits at y 852-1434 (582 px tall) and 7.3 at y 821-1466 (645 px tall), both 768 px wide, so 7.3 is offset by about 31 px at the top and 32 px at the bottom. At 300 DPI that is a step of about 2.6 mm between panels that sit side by side, and it is plainly visible in a zoomed crop and at reduced page size. The two images have different aspect ratios, and each is centred inside the same 163.1 pt row (LAYOUT-fitted-s1m2.json; page 7 rows were set by hand). That also leaves gutters of 24 to 56 px above and below tier 2, against 5 to 6 px everywhere else in the chapter. Every other side-by-side tier in ch12 lines up exactly (pages 1, 2, 4 and 5); only page 6 tier 1 is off, by about 5 px. Nothing is hidden: the lettering, speaker tails and action all read correctly. The fix is to re-fit or crop the layout so 7.2 and 7.3 share a height, with no redraw needed. That makes it polish, so minor.

confirmed.description: The two off-panel Ramayyan balloons have huge wedge tails. Both run from the panel's top-left corner across the whole image and slice through the fleeing family and the burning village, which are the key action of the memory panel.
confirmed.evidence: The tail of 'They burned villages. They took what they wanted.' runs from the top-left corner to the right-hand balloon, crossing the bundles and heads of the woman and the man on the bund. The tail of 'They sat on the edges...' is a second wide wedge from the same corner down over the family.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 2, panel 2.3. I zoomed into the full-resolution render. Both off-panel Ramayyan balloons have long, wide wedge tails that start at the panel's top-left corner. The upper tail, on "They burned villages. They took what they wanted.", runs about two-thirds of the way across the panel to the right-hand balloon. On the way it cuts through the woman's head bundle, the man's head and bundle, and the burning huts and lead horseman on the left side of the village. The lower tail, on "They sat on the edges...", is a second wide wedge from the same corner down to the left balloon. It covers the foliage and the edge of the woman's back and sari. Together the two white triangles make a large X-shaped wedge over the upper-left of the panel. That is where the script puts the key beat: "A family hurries away along a bund with bundles on their heads", with horsemen against the flames. Nothing in the script or bible asks for this. Script 2.3 marks the lines as RAMAYYAN (off), which only needs a short tail to the panel edge. The family and village are still recognisable and the text is legible, so this is not a blocker. It is a localized lettering fault that hides the panel's main action and would be obvious at print size, so it is major. Fix: use short tails to the nearest panel border, or tailless off-panel or caption-style balloons.

confirmed.description: The off-panel balloons sit over the walled town and the road, not the open sky the script asks for. The two Ramayyan tails are long wedges that converge on the top-right corner and cut diagonally across the town, the road and the hillside. 'Each time, men died' sits higher than 'He gave it up...', so the order of Ramayyan's two lines is ambiguous.
confirmed.evidence: 'He gave it up, then took it back...' (bottom centre) covers the lower town wall and gate. Its tail runs about 600 px up to the top-right corner, through the town. The top of 'Each time, men died...' is about 60 px above the top of 'He gave it up', on the right, which invites reading it first.

verdict.reason: Partly confirmed, but it is minor rather than major. I zoomed in on panel 4.3. The open sky the script asks for exists, but only the caption uses it. "He gave it up, then took it back..." sits over the bottom of the town: it hides the left half of the near gate arch and the stretch where the road comes in toward the viewer. Its tail is a long white wedge that runs from the balloon's top edge, through the middle of the town between the gopuram and the main road, up to the top-right corner. The "Each time" tail meets it at that same corner and crosses the plains and the right hillside. So the reviewer's description of the art is accurate. It still is not a major problem. The panel still reads clearly as a walled town at the mouth of a pass, with the gopuram, the walls and the road running out to the plains all visible. Both tails point off-panel toward the off-panel speaker, which the script allows, so neither tail is wrong. The reading-order complaint is weak. The top of "Each time" is only about 60 px higher (roughly 5 mm at print size) on balloons about 230 px tall. "He gave it up" sits directly under Nagoji's question on the left, so most readers will go there first. The wording also fixes the order: "He gave it up... again" comes before "Each time, men died". What remains is polish: move Ramayyan's two balloons up into the empty sky to either side of the caption, or join them with a connector, and shorten the tails so they do not cut across the town.

confirmed.description: Dhanaji's first balloon hides Nagoji's whole body. The scripted business, Nagoji standing and holding both bridles, is invisible: only his head and boots show.
confirmed.evidence: 'Their horse were better than ours...' is a large oval at panel centre. It covers Nagoji from the chin to the knees and covers the second horse's head and reins. Only the turban and face above it and the boots below it are visible.

verdict.reason: I confirm it as major. At full resolution, the "Their horse were better than ours..." oval on page 4, panel 4.2 sits right on top of Nagoji. Only his rust turban, his face and a sliver of red at the top of one shoulder show above it. Below it you see only his trouser legs from about mid-thigh, and his boots. The balloon hides his chest, his red sash, both arms and both hands. The reins of the horse on the right run straight into the balloon's edge, so you never see him holding them. The horse behind Dhanaji shows only its saddle and flank; its head and bridle are also behind the balloon. So the script's business for 4.2, "Nagoji stands holding both bridles", is not visible. At print size Nagoji reads as a floating head over a pair of legs, which is not a slight flaw. Nothing in the script or the continuity bible allows it. It is not a blocker: the dialogue reads, the tail points correctly at Dhanaji, his face identifies Nagoji, and the legs show he is standing. It is a lettering fix rather than a redraw. Shrink the balloon or move it into the free rock-and-foliage area at the top left, above Dhanaji's head, and the torso and bridles reappear. The reviewer's wording is a little loose ("chin to knees" is more like "neck to mid-thigh"), but the substance is right.

confirmed.description: The two captions blanket the top half of the closing panel. The top of Nagoji's head is cut off by the panel border, and 'So I kept my silence...' sits over his head and shoulders and over the black horizon he is meant to face. 'news.' is also left alone on a widow line.
confirmed.evidence: Nagoji, seen from behind on the right, shows only a strip of hair and turban tail between the panel top and the caption box (crop rows 15-95). The caption box then covers his neck and upper back (rows 95-225). The caption text breaks as '...watched the horizon for / news.'

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 4, panel 4.5, the closing panel. I zoomed into the render at page-04.png, around x 1080-1450 and y 2170-2300 at full resolution.

1. The top panel border cuts Nagoji's head at about ear level, so the crown of the turban and his eyes are gone. Only a band roughly 80 px tall is left (about 7 mm at print size), showing his ear, earring, cheek and moustache tip. The right caption, "So I kept my silence...", starts right under his jaw and covers his neck, shoulders and upper back. Read at page size, the caption cuts across his neck: a thin sliver of head sits above the box and his body below it. For the protagonist's last image in the sequence, that is a clear fault.
2. The script says "he stays facing the black horizon." That beat is weakened because his head direction and gaze are almost entirely cropped away or covered. The other beats still read: the wick being pinched out, with smoke rising, and Ramayyan and Dhanaji in the lit doorway are clear and uncovered.
3. One part of the claim is overstated. The art shows no real horizon: the background is dark fort walls and trees. So the caption does not hide a drawn horizon. The trouble is that it crowds his head.
4. The widow line is real ("...watched the horizon for / news."), but on its own it is only minor polish.

Nothing in the script or CONTINUITY.md allows the head crop or the caption sitting on the figure. Nagoji's identity still reads from the rust-red turban tail and red sash, so this is not a blocker. It is a localised framing and lettering fault. The fix is to reframe so his whole head shows under the border, then move or reflow the right caption so it no longer sits across his neck and shoulders. Reflowing it would also clear the widow.

confirmed.description: Ramayyan's long balloon covers Varma's body: his lean forward from the seat, his arm and the hand that should take the leaf. 'Fallen? Dead?' sits on the crown of Varma's head. Only Varma's face and one shoulder remain, so the hand-off beat does not read.
confirmed.evidence: 'Captured. The Marathas took Tiruchirappalli...' fills the right half of the panel from Varma's chin to the floor. Its tail stops at the pillar between the two men. The bottom of the 'Fallen? Dead?' balloon overlaps Varma's hair.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 6, panel 6.1 after zooming. Ramayyan's four-line balloon ("Captured. The Marathas took Tiruchirappalli...") takes up the lower right of the panel. It runs from just under Varma's gold necklaces down to the floor. Everything below his collarbone is hidden: his torso, his lap on the red cushion, and the near arm that would take the leaf. Only his head, neck, upper chest and his far shoulder and arm (screen right) are visible. The palm-leaf bundle in Ramayyan's hands ends right at the balloon's upper-left edge, so it seems to disappear into the balloon. The reader sees the leaf offered but never sees it received. The script's "Varma leaning forward from his seat" survives only as a forward-tilted head. The "Fallen? Dead?" balloon has a smaller problem. Its bottom outline clips the top of Varma's hair, and its tail tip lands on his forehead and temple instead of stopping short of him. The reviewer goes too far in saying the hand-off "does not read." Ramayyan's offering gesture and Varma's gaze toward him still show the intent, so this is not a missing beat and not a blocker. It is still a clear, localized lettering placement that hides half the action, and it would be obvious at print size. Severity is major. Fix by reflowing Ramayyan's text into a wider, shorter balloon placed over the roof beams or the open floor at bottom left, clear of Varma. Also raise "Fallen? Dead?" so its outline and tail stay off his head.

confirmed.description: The scripted business, Nagoji setting a gold coin on a stack from the brass tray, is hidden. The second balloon covers his torso, his hands and the table in front of him.
confirmed.evidence: 'The Marathas are patient. They will extract every pagoda...' covers the centre-right of the panel, from Nagoji's chest down past the table edge. No coin, stack or brass tray is visible anywhere in the panel.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed. The lettered panel on page 7 (right panel of row 2, panel 7.3) does hide the action. I cropped and zoomed the render: the table shows only the ola bundle and the ink pot. Nagoji's right forearm reaches down into the second balloon ("The Marathas are patient...") and disappears behind it. That balloon covers his hand, his red sash, and the centre and right of the table down to the mat.

The raw frame (chapters/ch12/frames/page-07-panel-03-v01.png) proves the art itself is correct. It shows Nagoji placing a gold coin on a small stack, with the brass tray of coins and a second ola bundle beside it, at exactly the spot the balloon now covers in the page render. So the scripted business ("setting one plain gold coin on a small stack from the brass tray") was drawn and then lost in lettering. Neither the script nor the bible allows dropping it. It is not too slight to matter: no coin, stack or tray is visible anywhere in the printed panel. The beat reads as Nagoji reaching toward nothing.

Severity is major rather than blocker. The dialogue still carries the story beat, and the fix is local: re-letter only. The plain wall in the upper right of the panel, above the Nair chieftain on the right, has room for the second balloon, with a short tail to Nagoji. The panel does not need to be redrawn.

confirmed.description: The chapter's last caption covers the centre of an already narrow final panel. It hides the long, empty pale beach that the script and the line itself ('the sand where we would meet them') make the subject of the closing image.
confirmed.evidence: The caption box takes up about 40% of the panel width, from just right of Nagoji's figure to the sea. Only a sliver of surf and sand shows at the far right edge, so no beach running into the dark can be read.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 8, panel 8.5. I measured the 300 DPI render. The panel's inner area runs from x 448 to 1388 and y 2240 to 2538. The caption box runs from x 877 to 1267 and y 2240 to 2488. That is about 41% of the panel's width (0.46 to 0.87) and the top 83% of its height, so it hides roughly a third of the art.

I checked this against the unlettered frame the manifest selected (chapters/ch12/frames/page-08-panel-05-v02.png). That frame was drawn with the scripted subject in exactly that zone. The long pale beach curves away from below the rise, past the palms, toward a dark headland in the distance, and its near surf line runs from about the middle of the frame to the far right. Almost all of that curve, the headland and the point where the beach disappears into the dark sit under the caption.

What still shows is the moonlit sea, the surf and a little sand in the right-hand strip (about 13% of the width), plus a thin band of rocks, scrub and grey sand under the box. One correction to the original report: it is not only a sliver at the right edge, because some pale sand shows along the bottom. Even so, the "long pale beach runs away into the dark, empty, waiting" from the 8.5 description, which the caption's own words "the sand where we would meet them" point to, cannot be read at print size. Nagoji walking back to the fires is still intact.

Nothing in the script or bible allows covering the beach. A fix only needs relettering: a wider, shallower caption over the empty sky in the upper middle (from about x 0.35 to 0.95, top 40%) would leave the beach curve visible. Because the problem is clearly wrong but localized and needs no redraw, the right severity is major, not blocker.

confirmed.description: Nagoji is not 'standing apart at the back beside a pillar'. He stands close behind the king's left shoulder, level with Ramayyan, as if he were part of the royal party. The script sets this up on purpose: in 6.2 and 6.5 every chief turns to look at the outsider at the far end of the hall, so in the art he seems to jump from beside the throne to the back. The panel is also drawn half-width rather than as the 'Wide' establishing shot, and Varma sits on a high-backed carved throne chair rather than on a low dais.
confirmed.evidence: Page 5, third row, left panel. Nagoji (rust turban, red sash, boots) stands at the right edge just behind Varma's throne. Ramayyan stands at the left, also beside the throne. Varma sits on a carved high-backed chair with a red cushion. Compare 6.2 and 6.5, where Nagoji stands alone in the centre aisle at the far end of the hall.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 5, panel 5.3 (third row, left). The zoomed crop shows Nagoji (rust turban, red sash, boots) standing on the raised throne platform, just behind and to one side of Varma's chair. He is at the same depth as Ramayyan on the other side, so the three read as one royal group: Ramayyan, the seated king and a bodyguard. The script asks for the opposite. 5.3 says "Nagoji standing apart at the back beside a pillar". 6.2 has every chief turn "toward the back of the hall" to look at him "by his pillar". 6.5 looks over Varma's shoulder at "Nagoji small at the far end beside his pillar". 7.1 has him "stepping forward from the pillar". The page 6 art follows the script: Nagoji stands alone in the centre aisle at the far end. That makes 5.3 the odd panel, and it gives away the outsider beat that 6.2 is built on. Neither CONTINUITY.md (Varma's 12 @5 row only covers his dress, the low dais and the spear) nor the cast overrides (5.3 lists nagoji, ramayyan and varma, with no position) allow the throne-side placement. He is large and easy to spot, so the problem is visible at print size. Two parts of the original report do not hold up. "Wide" in the script means a wide shot, not a full-width panel, and the half-width panel is a wide shot. The carved chair stands on a low red-carpeted platform, which is at most a minor departure from "seated on a low dais". The confirmed issue is the staging only: Nagoji should be moved to the far end of the hall by a pillar, away from the king. It is localized to one panel and needs a redraw, so the severity is major, not blocker.

confirmed.description: Varma is drawn standing on the dais steps with his spear. In the script he stays seated from 5.3 through 7.4: he reads in 6.3, is 'on the dais' in 7.2 and hands the ola down in 7.4. His rise, spear in hand, is held back as the closing beat of 7.5. Standing here uses up that rise early and makes him jump between standing and seated across 6.4, 7.2 and 7.4.
confirmed.evidence: Page 6, fourth row. Varma stands at full height on the wooden dais steps, gripping a spear, while the grey-haired chief mutters in the foreground. In 7.2 and 7.4 he is seated again, and 7.5 shows him 'rising'.

verdict.reason:
The finding is correct. I cropped the right half of page 6, panel 6.4. Varma is clearly standing at full height on the floor just in front of the dais steps, holding his spear upright in his right hand. He has the side knot, bare chest, cream and gold mundu and gold necklaces, so this is him and not another figure. His hands are empty: the ola he reads seated in 6.3 is gone, yet he is holding it again in 7.2.

The panels around it show him seated. In 6.3 he sits on the dais with the leaf. In 6.5 he is seen from behind at the eye level of the seated chiefs. In 7.2 and 7.4 he is plainly seated on the cushioned dais, and 7.4 shows his lap and mundu. In 7.5 he stands with the spear.

The script never lets him stand before 7.5. It has him "leaning forward from his seat" in 6.1, "on the dais ... beside his seat" in 7.2, handing the ola down in 7.4, and "Varma rising, spear in hand" as the closing beat in 7.5. The CONTINUITY row for Varma in chapter 12 (page 5 on) agrees: his spear is "at his right hand by the low dais, carried when he rises", so it is held only when he rises. The script for 6.4 only says he is "in the background, not troubling to look at him", which does not allow him to stand up and take the spear.

The figure is large, about a third of the panel width, so readers will see him go from seated to standing, back to seated, then rising again. That also spends the 7.5 rise early. It is a staging and prop continuity error confined to one panel. It needs a redraw of 6.4 with Varma seated on the dais in the background, holding the ola, spear leaning beside him. It is not an identity or lettering failure, so it is major rather than a blocker.

confirmed.description: The planned piece of business is missing. Nagoji is supposed to set a plain gold coin on a small stack from the brass tray as he talks, which pays off the coin tray planted in 5.3 and shows what a 'pagoda' is (adaptation note). No coin, stack or tray appears. Nagoji just sits cross-legged with an empty open hand, and his lower body is covered by the balloon.
confirmed.evidence: Page 7, second row, right panel. The low table holds a tied palm-leaf bundle and a small dark ink pot, with no brass tray and no coins. Nagoji's right hand is held out empty, and the 'The Marathas are patient...' balloon covers his lap and the table edge.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 7, panel 7.3 (second row, right). Script 7.3 calls for Nagoji to set "one plain gold coin on a small stack from the brass tray as he speaks". The adaptation notes say this business is how 7.3 shows what a pagoda is, and the checklist lists "business with the ola and the coins" for 7.2 to 7.4. I zoomed in on the panel. The low table holds only a tied palm-leaf bundle and a small dark pot with a stylus. There is no brass tray, coin or stack anywhere in the panel. Nagoji's right hand is out over the table edge, and it is empty. The large "The Marathas are patient..." balloon covers his lap and the right half of the table, where the coin business would sit. The bible and the cast overrides have nothing that allows leaving it out. One thing softens it: a brass tray of gold coins is visible in the panel next to it, on Varma's table in 7.2 (second row, left). So the prop is on the page, but nothing links it to the word "pagoda", and readers who do not know the term lose the planned gloss. The dialogue beat itself is intact and readable, so this is not a blocker. It is a localized staging miss, with the balloon sitting over the area where the action should be. Severity: major.

confirmed.description: The closing image does not match the script. Nagoji should have turned from the sea and be walking back toward the camp fires, which carries the novel's last line 'I turned back toward the camp'. He is drawn walking toward the camera, away from the fires, which are behind him on the left. The 'long pale beach... empty, waiting' is reduced to a thin strip at the right edge that the caption box mostly covers. The script calls for a full-width panel, but it is drawn as a narrow inset about 60% of the page width.
confirmed.evidence: Page 8, bottom panel. Nagoji walks toward the reader on a dirt path, with the tents and campfires behind his left shoulder. The caption box covers the middle and right of the panel, leaving only a sliver of moonlit surf at the right edge. The panel is much narrower than the page's full-width rows.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 8, panel 8.5 (crop at original pixels x 430-1410, y 2225-2560). Nagoji walks straight toward the camera on a dirt track. The tents, torches and cookfires are behind him: the camp group is behind his right shoulder (frame left) and more fires sit in the background to frame right. He is walking away from the camp, not back toward it. Script line 279 asks for "Nagoji has turned from the sea and is walking back toward the fires of the camp." The adaptation note at line 294 says this walk is what carries the novel's cut last line, "I turned back toward the camp." So the image reverses the one action the panel exists to show. After 8.2 (on the rise looking out to sea) it reads as him leaving camp, and the chapter's closing turn is lost. The beach sub-claim also holds. The caption box sits over the centre-right of the panel, and the moonlit surf and pale sand show only in a strip about 150 px wide at the right edge, with a little sand along the bottom right. The "long pale beach runs away into the dark, empty, waiting" does not come across. One part of the claim is overstated: the panel is about 680 of 855 display px, roughly 80% of the widest row (8.1), not 60%. Other panels on this page are also narrower than full width (8.2 is about 61%), so the width on its own is only a minor layout point. It is not a blocker because the caption beat is present and lettered correctly, and Nagoji's identity and costume are right. It is a clearly wrong, localized composition error: the direction of travel should be reversed (Nagoji seen from behind or in three-quarter view heading toward the fires, with the beach shown open and uncovered), so major.

refuted.description: A Nagoji look-alike appears in the vision panel, which by the script and the cast overrides must contain no Nagoji. The standing Maratha officer at top right wears an orange turban, a white angarkha, a coloured cloth waist sash and a sword, and has a thick curled moustache with a clean chin. Together these copy Nagoji's silhouette (red-orange turban plus sash plus curled moustache). Readers may take him for Nagoji, especially under the first-person caption 'the very power I had escaped'. The seated officer in the right foreground also wears an orange turban and a coloured waist sash. The script asks for white or saffron pagdis and no red sashes.
refuted.reason: I zoomed into page 8, panel 8.3. The standing officer at top right and the seated officer in the foreground both wear turbans with a median hue of about 20 degrees. That is saffron-orange and matches the saffron pennant in the same panel (about 21 degrees). Nagoji's turban and sash on this page measure about 12 degrees, a rust-red or crimson, in 8.1, 8.4 and 8.5. The script for 8.3 explicitly allows "white or saffron pagdis" and bans only red sashes. Both officers' waist sashes are the same dark saffron-brown, not red. CONTINUITY.md bans only Nagoji's rust-red turban and sash on Maratha figures in vision panels, so the art follows the script and the bible. The standing officer also lacks every feature that identifies Nagoji: the broad red sash worn diagonally over the shoulder, the long loose curly hair, the ear stud and the upturned handlebar moustache. At high zoom he has short hair under the pagdi, a heavier and older face, and a thick moustache that droops slightly rather than curling up. He is a small, shadowed figure cut off at the panel's right edge, in a scene that is plainly a vision (the captive in chains, coins being counted, the saffron pennant). At print size he does not read as Nagoji, so the claimed resemblance does not hold.

refuted.description: Varma's hair does not match the ch12 @5- bible row ("hair in a side knot above the LEFT ear"). Across the hall pages it is a bun on the crown or back of the head with long loose curls down his back, and its position changes from panel to panel.
refuted.reason: The claim does not hold up as stated. The bible row for ch12 @5- does require "a side knot above the LEFT ear", and the 6.5 prompt (chapters/ch12/prompts/page-06-panel-05.txt) asked for it. But the reviewer's main point, that no hall panel shows a left-side knot and that the knot moves from panel to panel, is wrong when you zoom in. Checking which ear is visible in each panel, the knot sits on his LEFT side, high and toward the back, in most of them. In 5.3 he faces the viewer and the knot is on the viewer's right, which is his left. In 5.5, 6.3 and 7.4 he is in profile facing left, so his left ear shows, and the bun sits just above and behind it. In 6.4 it is at the upper left of the crown. That matches how the "side knot" was drawn in the earlier chapter 7 frames (for example ch07/frames/page-08-panel-05-v02.png): a bun behind and above the left ear, with loose curls at the nape. So the chapter is consistent with the look already set, not drifting at random. The loose curls under the knot also appear in 5.5, 6.3, 6.4 and 7.4 and in ch07, so they are part of the established version, not a 6.5 error. The only real deviation is 6.5 itself. It is a rear over-the-shoulder view, and the bun sits on the crown, slightly toward his right, rather than on the viewer's left. In that view, at print size, Varma's head is about an inch tall, and the shape (a knot on top with long dark curls) reads the same as 6.4 directly above it. He is identified by the framing, the spear, the gold necklaces and the dialogue. A small shift of the knot in a back-of-head view is too slight to need a redraw, so this is refuted. (A separate observation, not part of this claim: 6.4 shows a silver-grey streak at the front of Varma's hair, which the bible does not give him. The continuity reviewer may want to check that.)

refuted.description: The standing Maratha officer in this vision panel is dressed close to Nagoji's commander look, though the script states that "the figure on the rise is not in this panel". He wears a saffron-orange turban, a matching orange waist sash, a white angarkha, a talwar at the sash and a thick moustache. In the dim tent light the orange reads near Nagoji's rust-red, and the bible keeps Maratha riders and officers away from his turban-and-sash pairing.
refuted.reason: The script allows this. Script 8.3 asks for "Maratha officers in white angarkhas and white or saffron pagdis, no red sashes". The bible (CONTINUITY.md, lines 161 and 175) only rules out Nagoji's rust-red turban paired with a red sash. I zoomed into the top-right of 8.3. The standing officer wears a saffron-orange pagdi that matches the saffron pennant at the tent door, and his cummerbund is orange-tan, not red. Sampled hue of the sash is about 26 degrees. Nagoji's red sash in 8.1 samples at about 13 degrees, and his turban in 8.4 is visibly a deeper rust-red. He also does not read as Nagoji. He is half-cropped at the panel edge and partly behind the caption, with a different face: a heavier, older moustache and no loose curly hair. He stands guard inside the tent, among other white-turbaned and saffron-turbaned Marathas counting coin, so nothing suggests the figure from the rise has stepped into the vision. At print size the saffron next to Nagoji's rust-red is a palette nuance, not a costume or identity error.

refuted.description: Ramayyan's balloon sits on Varma's chest, directly under Varma's face, and its short tail points at the ola passing between the two men, not at Ramayyan. A reader is likely to give the line to Varma.
refuted.reason: I'm refuting this as a major problem. I cropped and zoomed panel 7.4 on page 7, and the art does not show a tail aimed at the ola. The wedge on Ramayyan's balloon ("Then we have a window...") starts at the balloon's left edge and runs up and to the left. Its tip is at about (945, 1706) in the 1838x2775 render. That is in open sky about 55 px above the bundle in Varma's hand, not on it. Extend the tail's line and it reaches Ramayyan's collarbone and chin, so it is aimed at him. The tip stops about 65 px (about 5 mm at 300 DPI) from the edge of his white cloth. The tail is about 100 px long (about 0.34 in), easy to see, and points away from Varma. Varma's own line ("And while they extract?") sits above with its tail clearly on his face, so readers can tell his two balloons apart. Reading order is also fine: Varma's balloon is highest, then Nagoji's on the left, then Ramayyan's lower right. The reviewer is right that the balloon sits just under Varma's chin and that no balloon is near Ramayyan's head. That is a polish issue, not a misattribution a reader following the tail would make. Fix for polish: lengthen or re-aim the tail so it ends near Ramayyan's mouth, or move the balloon a little left and above the ola so it no longer sits under Varma's chin.

refuted.description: The silent reaction beat is changed. Ramayyan should be reading the opened ola, knuckles whitening while his face stays perfectly composed. Instead he grips a palm-leaf bundle that is still tied shut with cord, and his face is a hard scowl straight at the reader. In 5.3 he has already broken the wax, so the art now says he has not read the news yet, and his face gives away the emotion it is meant to hide.
refuted.reason:
I don't think this is a major problem. I zoomed into page 5, panel 5.4, and the script's beat still comes through.

- **Hands:** Both fists clamp the leaf hard on the table. The knuckles and tendons stand out clearly, which is the "knuckles whiten, fingers tighten" beat.
- **Face:** It sits at the top of the frame, set and stern, with a flat closed mouth and only a slight frown. There is no open mouth, no wide eyes and no sign of distress. It is not a dramatic scowl. It also matches his grim face in 5.5, so it reads as unchanged and composed. The script never asks for a neutral or smiling face.
- **Cord and seal:** The wax seal from 5.2 is gone in 5.4, which fits him having broken it in 5.3. Only the cord wrap is left. Palm-leaf ola letters are bound with cord and can be held that way. In 5.3 he is already shown looking at the leaf in his hands, and in 5.5 he holds the same cord-wrapped bundle while he gives the news. A reader following 5.3, then 5.4, then 5.5 won't think he hasn't read it yet.

At most there are two small polish points:
- The cord wrap could be shown loosened.
- His eyes could look down at the leaf instead of slightly toward the camera.

Neither changes the story beat or needs a redraw, so I count this as refuted.

minors.description: In this close-up, Nagoji's jaw and chin are hatched with visible stubble. The bible allows 'light stubble at most, captivity only'. In the commander-era close-ups (7.3, 8.4) and on the nagoji-v2 sheet his chin is clean.
minors.evidence: 3x zoom of page-07.png around (700-920, 400-560): stippled stubble texture across the cheek, jaw and under the lip, below the curled moustache.

minors.description: Varma's face and hairline differ from his other panels. Here he has a high, receding hairline, a heavier and older-looking face and a bun at the back of the crown. In 7.2, 7.4 and 7.5 he has thick wavy black hair low on the forehead and the leaner varma-v1 face. He is still recognisable, but he does not quite read as the same man.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-05.png around (1150-1690, 2140-2540): a receded temple hairline and a broad high forehead. Compare the page-07.png crop around (1260-1500, 1500-1700): a full wavy hairline.

minors.description: Nagoji's identifying features are cropped away. Of his head, only curly hair and the ear stud show: the panel's top edge cuts off the turban, and the 'So I kept my silence' caption covers the rest. He reads mostly as an arm and a red sash. His Ramayyan and Dhanaji, at the left, read clearly.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-04.png around (1100-1500, 2180-2330): only the hair, a red turban tail and the stud are visible above the caption box. The turban crown and face sit outside the panel or under the caption.

minors.description: There are two olas in the handover. Ramayyan already holds a cord-bound bundle and a stylus while Varma passes him a second bundle, so he cannot "take it and tuck it into the fold of his white cloth" as the script has it.
minors.evidence: 7.4 centre: Ramayyan's hands work a bound bundle at his waist with a stylus in his right hand. Varma's outstretched hand at right holds a separate bound bundle.

minors.description: The setting jumps: 7.3 puts the hall in front of a closed, plastered back wall with a weapon rack and a cream banner. The rest of the page (7.2, 7.4, 7.5) and pages 5 to 6 show an open colonnade onto the sea.
minors.evidence: 7.3 background: a flat beige wall, a rack of spears and a hanging banner. No pillars open to the sea, while 7.2 and 7.4 show the sea and ships through the columns.

minors.description: The shrine flips sides. Seating order is unchanged (Nagoji on the left, Ramayyan on the right), but the lit shrine and its lamps move from behind Ramayyan at right (3.1, 3.2) to behind Nagoji at left (3.3). Panel 2.4 has the same flip against 2.1 and 2.5.
minors.evidence: In 3.1 the deity niche and brass lamps are at the right edge behind Ramayyan, and in 3.2 the shrine pillar is at the right edge. In 3.3 the deity niche and stepped lamps are at the left edge behind Nagoji, with Ramayyan still on the right.

minors.description: The stone changes between panels. In 2.2 it is a small dark pebble turned in the fingertips. In 3.1 it is a large grey, egg-sized rock, and Ramayyan seems to be scratching it with a stylus. In 3.2 the thrown stone is a tiny dot again.
minors.evidence: 2.2: a walnut-sized dark stone between his fingertips. 3.1 (zoomed): a fist-sized pale grey rock in his left hand with a stylus-like point held to it in his right.

minors.description: The light by the Aramboli gate reads as a glass-chimney lantern on a post. Bible rule: in Travancore settings lamps are clay or brass with open wicks, and there are no glass lanterns.
minors.evidence: Zoomed: beside the timber gate, the flame sits inside a translucent cylindrical housing with a cap, mounted on a post. The second light further right is similar.

minors.description: The script calls for matchlocks. The Nair muskets read as hammer-lock (flintlock or percussion-style) guns with barrel bands: there is no serpentine holding a smouldering match cord, and the flash comes from a cocked hammer.
minors.evidence: Zoomed musket at the lower right of 4.1: a cocked hammer with fire at the lock, two brass barrel bands, and no match cord. The lower-left musketeer's gun shows the same lock.

minors.description: Varma reads a single palm leaf that carries faint rows of script-like marks. Standing rule: no text of any kind in the art, which is why the ola is drawn sealed.
minors.evidence: Zoomed leaf in Varma's hands in 6.3: several faint horizontal rows of dark glyph-like strokes along its length.

minors.description: Varma's forehead mark changes from panel to panel within one scene.
minors.evidence: 6.3 and 6.4: a red-and-white vertical namam. 7.5: a single small red dot. 5.5 and 7.4: a bare forehead.

minors.description: The panel's top border crops off Varma's peacock-feather crest, so the court look's signature crest (bible ch12 @1-4) does not read. Only the jewel at the turban front is visible.
minors.evidence: 1.5: the turban runs into the top frame line. A small jewel shows, but no peacock eye or feather.

minors.description: Ramayyan's stylus, lying on the step beside his palm-leaf bundle, reads as a modern pen or mechanical pencil. It has a smooth cylindrical barrel, a turned brass collar and a machined conical tip. A period Kerala ezhuthani is a plain iron stylus.
minors.evidence: page-02.png, bottom right of 2.2 (display coords around x 1040-1217, y 690-735, zoomed 6x). The barrel with a brass ferrule ring and cone point looks like a fountain pen or propelling pencil.

minors.description: On the Aramboli palisade beside the timber gate, one light is an enclosed cylindrical lantern with a flame visible through a translucent housing. It reads as a glass lantern in a Travancore setting. The other lights on the works are open torches, as the rule requires.
minors.evidence: page-03.png, 3.4, on the palisade post just left of the gate (display coords around x 720-790, y 1330-1420, zoomed 8x). A capped cylinder housing with a flame inside sits on a bracket.

minors.description: The ola Varma is reading is painted with faint parallel rows of dark strokes that read as lines of script. This is pseudo-text in the art. The script and the standing rules require the leaf to show no writing.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, 6.3, the leaf held across Varma's chest (display coords around x 600-800, y 790-845). Zoomed 4x, it shows rows of short dark marks running along the leaf like inscribed lines. The ola in 7.2 shows only plain grain.

minors.description: A soldier at the campfire, at the left edge behind Nagoji's face, wears a dark flat-topped peaked cap and a dark buttoned tunic with a leather crossbelt and belt pouch. He reads as a 19th-century European or forage-cap soldier, not a 1741 Nair (bare-headed, topknot, white mundu) or a Deccan rider (white pagdi).
minors.evidence: page-08.png, 8.4, left edge (display coords around x 256-330, y 1430-1560, zoomed 6x). The cap, dark uniform tunic, crossbelt and pouch are clear. A second figure in a similar cap sits beside him.

minors.description: In the Travancore camp background, a bare-headed bearded man wears a dark tailored jacket over a collared shirt with a sash. He reads as a European or modern figure, which does not fit the camp's Nair soldiers and Deccan riders.
minors.evidence: page-08.png, 8.1, upper left behind the tent poles (display coords around x 235-300, y 340-420, zoomed 8x). Visible are a dark lapelled coat, a light shirt with a standing collar and a reddish waist sash.

minors.description: 'We were weak, and Chanda Sahib knew it.' is squeezed into a tall, narrow balloon with one or two words per line, jammed against the right and bottom panel borders. The first balloon covers Nagoji's lap and the talwar laid across his knees.
minors.evidence: The text breaks as 'We were / weak, / and / Chanda / Sahib / knew it.' The balloon's right edge touches the panel border. 'He came first in thirty-six...' sits over Nagoji's knees and the sword.

minors.description: Three balloons ring Nagoji's face. The left one breaks into two- or three-word lines and runs up into the panel top, where the top of his turban is also cut off.
minors.evidence: 'I knew Raghuji / Bhonsle was / ambitious and that...' is a narrow column that touches the top border. 'But I did not know...' and 'I have been here, Maharaja...' crowd in on his cheek and chin.

minors.description: The reading order is ambiguous. Ramayyan's first line is at top right, and Nagoji's reply is at left, a little lower, so a left-to-right reader may start with Nagoji. The balloons also sit over the palisade and gate, not in the 'generous sky' the script asks for.
minors.evidence: The top of 'The Maharaja understood that tribute buys time...' is at about display y 1300 on the right. 'I have seen them. From a distance.' is at left, at about y 1420. 'You will see them closer.' is at bottom right.

minors.description: 'How many times?' overlaps the left side of Nagoji's turban, and the panel top crops its crown. Ramayyan's balloon covers Nagoji's torso and hands. He is reduced to a face boxed in between two balloons.
minors.evidence: The 'How many times?' balloon overlaps the turban edge. 'Every year since. Sometimes Chanda Sahib himself...' spans from Nagoji's chest to the talwar on his knees.

minors.description: Nagoji, the principal holding the ravine mouth, is jammed into the top-left corner with the top of his turban cut off by the panel border. The caption sits directly under him over his horse.
minors.evidence: The turban crown is cut at the top border. 'We spoke of it afterward with the frustrated respect...' covers the horse's chest and Nagoji's leg.

minors.description: The grid is untidy. 6.3 and 6.5 are inset from the column, and in the top tier 6.1 and 6.2 do not share top or bottom border lines (they are off by a few px).
minors.evidence: 6.3 measures 1349 px and 6.5 measures 1310 px wide, against the 1540 px column used by 6.1/6.2 and 6.4. In the join crop, 6.1's bottom border sits about 7 px below 6.2's.

minors.description: Caption boxes butt directly onto the panel borders, sharing the border line. The approved Ch1 r6 standard insets every caption about 15 px inside the panel frame.
minors.evidence: The top edge of the 1.1 caption 'Before the Dutch became the enemy...' is the panel's top border line. The 1.2 caption is flush in the top-left corner. Ch1 page 1 panel 1 'The first thing they took was my name.' has a clear gap of art above and left of the box.

minors.description: The tail of 'And he came?' stops on the stone pillar, well short of Nagoji, so it points at the architecture, not the speaker.
minors.evidence: The tail tip ends at about display (360, 1205) on the pillar edge, about 150 px left of Nagoji's turban and face.

minors.description: The two captions cut Nagoji's figure in half (torso, then sash and legs), and the second caption is wedged into the bottom-right corner against both borders.
minors.evidence: 'I thought of the Maratha sardars...' covers Nagoji's chest and arm. 'We called it our right...' covers his sash and lower body and touches the right and bottom panel borders.

minors.description: Ramayyan is not 'lowering the leaf and turning to Varma'. He holds a stylus poised over the still-bound bundle, as if taking notes (the stance from his character sheet), and his body faces the reader rather than the king.
minors.evidence: Page 5, bottom panel. In his right hand a stylus touches a cord-tied bundle in his left. His torso faces out of the panel, and Varma sits at the right edge, chin on hand.

minors.description: The script says 'Every chief's head turned over his shoulder toward the back of the hall'. The two most prominent foreground chiefs look sideways and out of the panel instead of toward Nagoji, which weakens the beat in which the whole room remembers where he came from.
minors.evidence: Page 6, top right panel. In the left foreground the moustached chief looks toward the camera and the grey-bearded chief looks off to the right. Only the chiefs at the right and in the middle distance turn toward Nagoji at the far end.

minors.description: The hand-back of the ola is unclear. Ramayyan already holds his own tied bundle and stylus and looks down at it, while Varma holds out a second bundle that no one takes. Two olas appear, and the action of taking it and tucking it into his cloth does not come across. The balloon order is also shaky: Nagoji's answer, 'While they extract...', sits at upper left, roughly level with Varma's question, 'And while they extract?', at upper right, so a reader may read the answer first.
minors.evidence: Page 7, third row. One bundle is in Ramayyan's hands with a stylus and a second is in Varma's outstretched hand. Nagoji's balloon is at the far left, starting just below the bottom of Varma's balloon at top right.

minors.description: Varma should already have turned toward the open side of the hall and the sea, which turns the chapter toward the coming fight. Instead he faces the camera and the chiefs, with the sea behind him.
minors.evidence: Page 7, bottom panel. Varma stands frontally on the dais, looking toward the left foreground. The ships and sea are behind his back.

minors.description: The framing differs from the script. It calls for a low angle with the commander backlit so his face is lost in shadow, and the banner bearer a length behind him. The art is an eye-level or high rear view in full daylight, with the banner bearer riding level with him on the left.
minors.evidence: Page 1, second row, right panel. The camera looks slightly down across the rocks at the backs of both riders. The sun is upper right and Chanda Sahib's jama is evenly lit. The bearer with the dark flag rides beside him, not behind.

minors.description: The Deccan memory does not 'bleed in like a stain'. It continues seamlessly from the shrine scene with the same colour and light and no vignette or edge treatment, so the Maratha riders and the farmer look as if they are physically passing beside the Travancore shrine rather than being remembered.
minors.evidence: Page 2, bottom panel. The stubble field with riders and a saffron pennant runs directly into the laterite steps where Nagoji sits, under one continuous sunset sky.

minors.description: Ramayyan's first balloon sits on top of his head and its tail ends between his eyes, hiding his receding hairline (his main identifying feature) and jabbing into his face.
minors.evidence: Page 2, fourth row. The bottom edge of the 'He had no choice...' balloon cuts across Ramayyan's forehead, and the tail tip lands on the bridge of his nose.

minors.description: Ramayyan is not turning the small stone from 2.2. He holds a fist-sized rock and scratches at it with a stylus, as if writing on it. The stone then shrinks back to a pebble in 3.2.
minors.evidence: Page 3, top panel. A large grey egg-shaped rock sits in his left hand, with a stylus in his right touching it. In 2.2 the stone was a small pebble between his fingers.

minors.description: The throw reads as pointing. The stone is a barely visible speck at the top edge, so 3.2 and 3.3 (where Ramayyan points at the hills) look like two pointing panels in a row. The panel is also fully lit rather than 'almost silhouette'.
minors.evidence: Page 3, second row. Ramayyan's arm is raised with an open hand, and a tiny dark dot with a faint trail sits near the top right border. Both figures are lit in full colour against the sunset.

minors.description: Dhanaji should gesture at the rocks, gullies and hills to support 'We let the land fight for us'. He only wipes his face, and Nagoji holding both bridles is hidden behind the large balloon.
minors.evidence: Page 4, second row, left panel. Dhanaji holds a cloth to his eye with one hand and his other arm rests at his side. Nagoji's hands and the reins are covered by the 'Their horse were better...' balloon.

minors.description: Nagoji's head is cut off by the top border and the second caption box, and he faces left into the fort yard rather than staying 'facing the black horizon' after he puts out the lamp.
minors.evidence: Page 4, bottom panel. Only an ear and a strand of turban tail show above the 'So I kept my silence...' caption. His body is turned toward the lamp and the yard at the left.

minors.description: The panel is not drawn as a vision bleeding across the night sky above the sea. It is a straight interior shot of the tent with no sky or sea, so it reads as a hard cut to the Carnatic rather than as Nagoji's imagining.
minors.evidence: Page 8, middle panel. The full frame is a lamplit tent interior with the captive, officers and coins. No night sky, sea or fading edge appears.
